recentItems.title: Spring Day water-splashing: Harmless fun or public harassment?
recentItems.description:
Spring Day water-splashing is traditionally seen as harmless fun, especially among young people marking the start of the season.

But the tradition is increasingly raising questions about respect, responsibility and public safety. 

Unsuspecting motorists, schoolchildren and elderly people have been targeted, while this year's celebrations have been marred by serious confrontations, including a reported fatal stabbing.

So, when does playful behaviour cross the line into something dangerous, and why do some young people take these celebrations too far?

For more on the psychology behind this behaviour and the risks involved, we speak to University of Johannesburg Senior Lecturer and Educational Psychologist, Dr Nancy Mabaso.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Aviation | What happens when aviation emergencies strike?
recentItems.description:
Recent aviation incidents are raising questions about South Africa's readiness when things go wrong.

A burst tire on a Kenya Airways aircraft closed Cape Town International's runway for hours, while rugby flyovers were cancelled amid concerns over an Airlink passenger aircraft flying at a potentially unsafe altitude above a stadium of more than 55,000 people.

The incidents highlight wider concerns around emergency response, regulatory compliance, and airspace safety—and raise a crucial question: Is South Africa adequately prepared to prevent and respond to aviation emergencies?

We discuss this with Volker von Widdern, Director of Strategic Risk at Riskonet Africa.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Traditional healers gather to celebrate African medicine and cultural heritage  at Malombo festival
recentItems.description:
September has ushered in a new season and with it, new beginnings across various traditions. 

In Polokwane, African traditional medicine practitioners are marking the start of the African New Year with the ancestral dance festival, Malombo.

The gathering is dedicated to promoting and preserving African Indigenous Knowledge Systems, traditional medicine and cultural heritage, bringing together traditional leaders, and government. 

SABC News reporter Katlego Nyoni has more details from Polokwane.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Major 4x4, outdoor, and overlanding gathering underway at Zwartkops Raceway
recentItems.description:
Thousands of outdoor, adventure, and motoring enthusiasts are gathering for the South African 4x4 & Outdoor Show at the Zwartkops Raceway in Centurion. 

The event is expected to attract more than 20,000 attendees, with visitors and exhibitors coming from across South Africa and internationally.

Visitors will experience live military and Special Forces demonstrations, skydiving displays, helicopter action, drifting, off-road driving, and access to five different active tracks.

For more on this we are now joined by SABC News reporter Luyanda Danca.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: UNAIDS, SADC, SANAC, and GHII complete five-day exchange with China's government
recentItems.description:
UNAIDS, SADC, the South Africa National AIDS Council and the Global Health Innovations Institute facilitated a five-day exchange between the Government of China, Chinese pharmaceutical manufacturers and regional partners, exploring how African manufacturing capacity can be strengthened and connected to technology, investment, predictable markets,  and regional procurement. 

The exchange comes as countries across the region seek to strengthen health security, reduce vulnerability to global supply disruptions, and build more sustainable access to medicines, diagnostics, and prevention technologies. 

At the conclusions of the five-day mission, participants will brief the media today on what was achieved, the practical opportunities identified, and the partnerships and next steps to be pursued. 

For more on this, we are joined by Senior Programme Officer for Health at the SADC Secretariat, Dr Lamboly Kumboneki.  

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Basic Education Minister Gwarube: Plans on track to ease school principals’ administrative burden
recentItems.description:
Basic Education Minister, Siviwe Gwarube, says her department's plans to reduce the administrative burdens faced by principals are in order.

Gwarube addressed the South African Principals Association national conference in Polokwane, Limpopo.

The three-day conference discussed ways to improve learning outcomes by reducing the administrative burdens for school principals.

SABC News reporter Katlego Nyoni reports.

recentItems.title: Thousands converge on Moria for annual September prayers: Katlego Nyoni reports
recentItems.description:
With the start of Spring, ZCC members are expected to converge on Moria in Limpopo to mark the beginning of "the new year". The church marks the new season with September prayers. 

Traffic is expected to peak as church members mark the occasion; ZCC Spokesperson Moatshe Ngoepe says they're expecting a high number of buses.

Ngoepe says that private vehicles and informal trading will not be allowed near the vicinity of Moria and says the precautions have been taken in the interest of public safety.

The church says they are necessary to protect worshippers and other road users, and to maintain order during the period of the gathering. 

For more on this, we're joined by SABC News reporter Katlego Nyoni in Polokwane.

recentItems.title: US attacks UN World Conference Against Racism
recentItems.description:
The United States has launched a blistering attack on the legacy of the 2001 United Nations World Conference Against Racism in Durban, weeks before the United Nations holds a high-level meeting to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the declaration adopted there.

The General Assembly is due to mark the anniversary on September 28, with the United Nations describing the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action as a global blueprint for racial justice and equality, and calling for renewed support for its full implementation.

SABC News correspondent Sherwin Bryce-Pease reports on some of the pushback to the U.S. position, with roughly two-thirds of UN member states continuing to support the implementation of the conference's outcomes.
